notesStmt.note: "Fancies at Navesink" was first published in The Nineteenth Century magazine in August 1885, meaning that this mansucript was written sometime prior to that date, likely in the early 1880s.

These draft lines contain vague similarities to several of the poems in the "Fancies at Navesink" cluster of November Boughs (1888), particularly "Last of Ebb, and Daylight Waning" and "Ye Tides With Ceaseless Swell," both of which, like these lines, deal with the ebb and flow of the tides.

lg.l:
What fiat ? sends ye out and
calls ye back again

What endless subtleintermutual chains to
to sun and moon? and stars?
in compact hold
